hz2_invasion.topic: Operation Peace for Galilee, the siege of Beirut, Sabra and Shatila, 1982

claims.text: Shlomo Argov, Israel's ambassador in London, was shot and severely injured on 3 June 1982 by a militant of the Abu Nidal Organization; the attempt led to Operation Peace for Galilee; he died of his injuries in 2003
Arutz Sheva (2003): Israeli jets bombed PLO depots and bases the day after the shooting; the PLO shelled northern Israel; the IDF launched the operation on 6 June

IDF official account: operation launched 6 June 1982 'following the attempted assassination of the Israeli Ambassador to the UK'; objective 'pushing the latter 40 km to the north'; war lasted more than three months; siege of Beirut hardened from late June; evacuation by sea under an international force completed 31 August

Begin Heritage Center: operation 'designed to harm terror organizations and ensure that the forty miles surrounding the border would be terrorist-free'; IDF 'was forced to continue north all the way to Beirut'; Arafat forced to leave in August; IDF later withdrew to the security zone
9 June 1982: Israeli Air Force destroyed 17 of 19 Syrian SAM batteries in the Bekaa (Mole Cricket 19); 13 June IDF reached West Beirut
MNF of US, French and Italian troops arrived in Beirut 24 August 1982 to oversee the PLO withdrawal
Marines withdrew 10 September 1982 after the PLO left; redeployed 29 September 1982 after the Sabra and Shatila massacre (16-18 September); the invasion had tacit US approval

Sabra and Shatila: Kataeb (Phalange) members killed between 762 and 3,500 civilians, mostly Palestinians and Lebanese Shia, in camps Israeli troops had surrounded; presented as retaliation for the assassination of president-elect Bachir Gemayel; 400,000 marched in Israel on 25 September 1982 demanding Begin's resignation
NJOP gives 656 Israelis killed in action and 3,887 wounded (window not stated) and stated aim 'pushing the PLO 40 KM further north'

hz2_founding.topic: IRGC in the Bekaa, Islamic Amal, Iran's role in its own words

claims.text: In 1982 Iran established a base in the Syrian-controlled Bekaa; from there the IRGC founded, financed, trained and equipped Hezbollah; the Sheikh Abdullah barracks in Baalbek was believed to house IRGC trainers; no troop numbers given

Hussein Musawi led Islamic Amal, a breakaway faction of Amal and an autonomous part of embryonic Hezbollah; no consensus whether Hezbollah existed at the time of the 1983 bombing; Hezbollah announced its existence in 1985
Belfer (2026): Hezbollah 'Founded in 1982 under Iranian Revolutionary Guard sponsorship'

Sayyed Issa Tabatabai, Khamenei's representative in Lebanon, told IRNA Hezbollah's efforts 'started in [Lebanon's] Baalbek area' where IRGC members arrived; '[Hezbollah's] military base was located in my home' for two years; he 'quickly went to Lebanon and provided what was needed'; IRNA removed part of the interview; MEMRI: Iran 'has always vehemently denied any role in the bombings'

Peterson (2003) found Hezbollah 'was formed under the auspices of the government of Iran'; expert Clawson: 'Hezbollah is largely under Iranian orders'; Paz: 'totally controlled by Iran'; Hezbollah 'received massive material and technical support from the Iranian government'; findings made after Iran defaulted
Fadlallah was later named by Lebanese and US officials as having blessed the 1983 bombers; he denied any role until his death in 2010; he became a grand ayatollah
CIA note after the September 1984 embassy annex bombing referred to 'Hizb Allah, operating with Iranian support under the cover name of Islamic Jihad'

hz2_1983.topic: 1983 embassy and barracks bombings, attribution, US court findings, denials, withdrawal

claims.text: 18 April 1983: suicide bombing of the US embassy in Ain al-Mraiseh, Beirut, killed 63 including 17 Americans
23 October 1983 about 06:22: truck bombs hit the Marine barracks and French Drakkar building; 241 US personnel (220 Marines, 18 sailors, 3 soldiers), 58 French paratroopers, 6 civilians killed

Two callers claimed the bombing in the name of the Islamic Jihad Organization; a statement to As-Safir claimed it for the 'Islamic Revolution Movement'; Syria, Iran and Amal denied involvement; the US initially blamed Amal and Islamic Amal
Hezbollah officially denied involvement but praised the 'two martyr mujahideen'; Hezbollah, Iran and Syria have continued to deny involvement

Peterson (Lamberth, 30 May 2003) held Iran and MOIS liable; findings: Hezbollah formed under Iranian auspices; MOIS message to the Iranian ambassador to Syria to 'take a spectacular action against the United States Marines'; meeting in Baalbek at the ambassador's direction planned simultaneous attacks on US and French barracks; truck 'driven by an Iranian member of Hezbollah'; blast 15,000-21,000 lb TNT; defendants defaulted; evidence must be 'satisfactory to the court'
NSA intercept of 26 September 1983 not passed to the Marines until 26 October
7 September 2007: Lamberth awarded about $2.66 billion; Iran called it 'baseless' and 'politically motivated'

20 April 2016: Supreme Court 6-2 upheld 2012 law directing about $2bn of Bank Markazi assets to more than 1,300 relatives; Iran called it 'theft'; Iran denies links to the bombing; ICJ 30 March 2023 lacked jurisdiction over Bank Markazi funds but found other US measures breached the 1955 treaty
Pence (23 Oct 2017) called the bombing 'the opening salvo' of the war on terror and Hezbollah a proxy of Iran

Long Commission blamed the military chain of command; a 'prevalent view' among commanders linked Navy shelling at Suq al-Gharb (Sept 1983) to the attack; Muslims believed the MNF sided with Maronites; Berri asked US and France to leave

17 May agreement signed 17 May 1983; IDF withdrew from Aley and Shouf 4 Sept 1983; USS New Jersey fired at Druze and Syrian positions 14 Dec 1983 and 8 Feb 1984; Reagan ordered withdrawal 7 Feb 1984; completed 26 Feb 1984; France struck alleged IRGC positions in the Bekaa

8 March 1985 car bomb in Beirut's Shia sector aimed at Fadlallah killed 80 civilians, wounded over 250; CIA denied role (backed by House Intelligence Committee); Woodward reported a Casey-Bandar operation with $3m Saudi money

hz2_letter.topic: The 1985 Open Letter, the 2009 manifesto, Israel's 1985 withdrawal

claims.text: Open Letter read 16 February 1985 by spokesman Ibrahim al-Amin at the al-Ouzai mosque in west Beirut; published in al-Safir as an open letter to the oppressed in Lebanon and the world; printed 22 February

Letter text: 'We see in Israel the vanguard of the United States in our Islamic world'; 'our struggle will end only when this entity is obliterated'; 'We recognize no treaty with it, no cease fire, and no peace agreements'; warns of 'Great Israel, from the Euphrates to the Nile'
Wikipedia footnote: the obliteration line is reportedly in the Arabic original but not in a translation and not on Hezbollah's website

Letter: calls the US 'that arrogant superpower'; aims to expel 'Americans, the French and their allies definitely from Lebanon'; Phalanges to be brought to justice; 'We obey the orders of one leader, wise and just' (Khomeini); people to choose 'in all the liberty the form of government'; 'Only an Islamic regime can stop' imperialist infiltration

Belfer: the letter rejected confessional power-sharing, aimed at a borderless Islamic republic, enshrined obedience to Khomeini; 2009 Political Document (52 pages, November 2009) renounced the immediate demand for an Islamic state, accepted consociational democracy, and set the 'Army-People-Resistance' equation

Nasrallah (2009): Hezbollah accepts 'consensus democracy' until sectarianism is abolished; defensive strategy relying on 'popular resistance' with the national army; Islamic Republic 'no longer a priority'; drafted not to recant the 1985 letter
Nasrallah reading the 2009 manifesto: 'Our problem with [the Israelis] is not that they are Jews, but that they are occupiers'
Israel to the UN (29 Feb 2000) cited Hezbollah's programme as stating 'the complete destruction of the State of Israel' as its goal and called Hezbollah a terrorist organization
Begin Center: 'some time later, the IDF withdrew to the security zone in southern Lebanon'

hz2_fill.topic: Kahan Commission, 1982 death tolls, IRGC contingent size, 17 May agreement, 1985 withdrawal

claims.text: Kahan Commission (Kahan, Barak, Efrat) report released 8 February 1983: massacre carried out by a Phalangist unit; no Israeli directly responsible; Israel indirectly responsible; Sharon responsible for 'ignoring the danger of bloodshed'; recommended the Defence Minister resign; DMI not continue in post
Kahan report: 'According to I.D.F. intelligence sources, the number of victims of the massacre is between 700 and 800' ... 'may well be the number most closely corresponding with reality'

CSM 9 Feb 1983: commission placed direct responsibility on the Phalangist militia allied with Israel; Sharon bore 'personal responsibility'; recommended Begin sack Sharon if he did not resign; Chief of Staff Eitan severely criticized but not recommended for dismissal as due to retire

Kahan Commission found Sharon bore 'personal responsibility' for 'ignoring the danger of bloodshed and revenge'; he initially refused to resign; after the Peace Now march and grenade attack he resigned as defence minister, staying as minister without portfolio
CSM 14 Feb 1983: Sharon kept in cabinet as minister without portfolio; Begin to take defence portfolio; a grenade attack killed a Peace Now demonstrator calling for implementation of the report

Emil Grunzweig killed 10 February 1983 by a grenade thrown by Yonah Avrushmi at a Peace Now rally outside the PM's office in Jerusalem; Avrushmi convicted of murder 1985, life sentence commuted to 27 years, released 2011
Lebanese government (Oct 1982): 762 bodies recovered from the camps; some 1,200 more buried privately by relatives; total close to 2,000; not independently verifiable
Al Jazeera (Battah 2012): Kahan estimated about 800; researchers incl. Amnon Kapeliouk closer to 3,500
PalQuest (Institute for Palestine Studies): more than 3,000 killed; some sources 4,000-4,500; 'almost certain' no less than 3,500; bulldozers and mass graves hamper counting
CSM 18 Nov 1982: 17,825 killed and 30,103 wounded in Lebanon 6 June-25 Aug 1982 per 'best available sources'; an-Nahar: 5,515 killed in Beirut; Israeli Army: 330 soldiers killed

CSM 21 Dec 1982: Lebanese police: 19,085 killed, 30,302 wounded 4 June-31 Aug 1982; Beirut 6,775 dead, 84% civilians; south ~20% civilians; Israeli Army: 446 soldiers killed, 2,383 wounded 4 June-19 Nov 1982
Israel MOD archives: '353 soldiers lost their lives in the warfare' (1982)
CSM 4 June 1985, citing Israeli Army spokesman: 654 Israeli soldiers killed in Lebanon, 3,195 wounded, 4 missing
Wilson Center: Iran dispatched 'some 1,500 IRGC trainers and advisers' to the Bekaa in 1982
USIP Iran Primer: within weeks of 6 June 1982 Iran deployed 1,500 IRGC advisers to the Bekaa
PBS Frontline/World: Iran sent 1,000 Revolutionary Guards to Lebanon at the conclusion of the Israeli siege
Wikipedia cites 1,500 to Library of Congress country study (Mason, 1989) and Shatz (NYRB 2004); its 800 figure is cited to Beinin MERIP 1993, which on checking does not mention the Guards
Al Majalla (Hamidi 2024): Iran sent 'a brigade and experts' of the IRGC via Syria, mostly to Sheikh Abdullah barracks in Baalbek; no number

17 May 1983 agreement text: state of war 'terminated'; border inviolable; Israeli withdrawal within 8-12 weeks of entry into force; Security Region in south; Joint Liaison Committee with US participation; no use of territory for hostile activity; prevent irregular forces; no hostile propaganda
Moubayed: liaison offices not embassies; Lebanese parliament approved June 1983 (2 against, 3 abstentions of 72 present); Assad rejected it; Lebanese government repudiated it 5 March 1984
Israeli withdrawal contingent on Syrian withdrawal; Lebanon repudiated the agreement 5 March 1984; parliament revoked it 21 May 1987
Israeli cabinet 14 January 1985: redeployment in three phases; final phase along the border keeping a zone where SLA operates with IDF backing
Phases: 16 Feb 1985 Sidon handed to Lebanese army; 24 April Bekaa; 29 April Tyre and pullback to security zone; 10 June 1985 most IDF troops left, small force stayed to support SLA
CSM 22 April 1985: cabinet voted to end occupation by first week of June
